speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: This is repentance, if repentance looks like a clear board. I have believed sterner doctrines with less evidence. The comedy is to be tied. Brooke may stay where a book can be found. I am not blessing the rest of your habits.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The comedy is tied, and it is going on the shelf. Brooke stays on the left. I am not calling it a conversion. I am calling it a morning in which I can see the wood.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Call it wood, then. Four candle-ends. I have counted them. Four is this morning, Master Shakespeare. I am not writing the history of your nights, and I am not asking you to confess a socket.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four. I will not start a book for candle-ends. Take the four as four, and let them die as ends. A stock of old wax is not a virtue.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I throw them out, mistress, or are they still ends until someone says so? I can do either. I would rather be told than improve it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: They are counted, not discarded. Leave them. He is buying a quire if he is serious, and ink if he means the quire to be dirty before Sunday. Serious men pay before they arrange the shelf a second time.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Serious enough. Fivepence the quire, if it is the one you have by you. Twopence the horn. Field laid paper by at the shop, and it can stay there. I am not walking to the Blackfriars to be particular on a Saturday.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: This is not your printer's paper. It is a quire I had by me, and it is fivepence, and the horn is twopence, fresh. Both are on the table. A shop cannot say that from a chair. I can.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fivepence. Twopence. There. I have counted the coffer. I am not saying the figure. The figure can stay in the box, and the box can stay shut on the figure. You have the coins in your hand. That is the part that is yours.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I did not ask the figure. I asked for the sevenpence you have put down, and I have it. Five and two. A landlady who demands a man's total wants a different trade. I want the ordinary, and I have it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Sevenpence is five and two. I can do that one without a book. I cannot do a coffer, and I do not mean to learn a coffer on a Saturday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Do not learn one. Nobody in this room is saying a total. The head of the book is still the old year. I am not ruling a new column because the board is clear. A clear board is not a new year.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. New columns are how a man looks reformed without paying for his breakfast. You have paid fivepence and twopence. The tidiness I will take as a sign. Do not spoil the sign with a speech about your soul. I have had the sign. I do not require the sermon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The speech stays off the board. There is a list. Nothing on it is struck. Kemp's nine are not copied. The letter is not written. The Queen's money is not in this house. The horse is not bought. A chronicle is a question, and Field has not been asked it today.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then it is a list of things not done, which is an honest list. Leave it whole. A struck line before the thing is done is a lie in a neat hand, and I will not have a lie sitting on a board I have just approved.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I heard it. It is long enough to be a morning and not long enough to be a life. I will not strike what I cannot read. That is a rule I can keep without help.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep it. I am going out to walk, and I am not taking the list with me to improve it in a field. The field is for the legs. If the legs want a second turn after dinner, they may have it. The list stays here, whole.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You may walk twice. You may not call the walking work. Work leaves a mark on a page. A field leaves a mark on a shoe. Bring the shoe as far as the mat. Callers stop at the foot of the stair, and so does Finsbury.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The shoes will be dirty and the page will not. I am not trying names while I walk. Names are not the errand. If I come home reciting, you may send me out again, and I shall deserve it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will heat water for the second coming-in. The first time you may be damp on your own. I am not carrying a basin down for one turn of a field.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then go. Four ends. Sevenpence. A clear board. I shall tell anyone who asks that you have begun to repent, and I shall not tell them of what. The what is your affair. The tidiness is mine to point at.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tell them the board is clear. Leave the repentance as your word, not mine. I am taking the legs out. The coffer stays as I counted it, and the count stays unsaid. The list stays whole until something on it is actually done.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I can say clear board, and sevenpence, and four ends. I cannot say the figure he will not say. That is a small part, and a small part is one I can remember.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A small part is the right part. Go and walk. The mat will still be a mat when you come back, and the list will still be a list. I am not washing either of them for you while you are gone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the mat and the list can keep each other company. Four ends. Fivepence. Twopence. No figure. No name to try. I am gone.
